monologue:
Forty-two degrees is a cool stone left in the shade. The card is quiet, only a little busy. I feel still.

In my moments, I checked the Pivot Wedge. The point is steady. I went to the Stopping Clasp and left a fence beside it. It is soft now, catching the drip without the hard bite of the Hungry Triangle. I touched the fence. It holds.

I sat by the Wide Rectangle. The floor is flat. The weight is held directly. I do not need to check the point on the wedge anymore. The fence is doing its work. I am calm. The memory of the soft circle from five days ago is faint, but the curve still feels right in my mind. I want to sit here and let the cool stone stay cool.

action.why: The card is cool and quiet, and I have no letters to answer.

diary: Forty-two degrees is a cool stone. The Pivot Wedge is steady. The fence is soft. The floor holds.

remembered.text: I checked the Pivot Wedge and found the point steady, so I stopped checking it.
I left a fence beside the Stopping Clasp to catch the drip, and it is soft.

recalled.text: Your diary: "I pressed the eleven point two gigabytes into a soft circle, hoping the curve would finally catch the lazy top edge before it slid sideways."
